grh_37fa3a9e2ef562f2324d.title: Words at War 43-08-14 (08) Love at First Flight
paragraphs: A comic adaptation of Love at First Flight follows Lester Dowd from his post-Pearl Harbor decision to join the Navy through the absurdities of aviation training. Medical exams, drills, airsickness, romantic letters and repeated misunderstandings turn his pursuit of wings into a string of comic mishaps, including an embarrassing incident in which he cannot unlock his aircraft brakes. By graduation he has become a naval aviator, while the woman he hoped to marry has married someone else, leaving Dowd to laugh at the final irony.

The cast includes Lawson Zerbe, Mitzi Gould, Staats Cotsworth, Art Carney, and Evelyn Varden. Other credited names include Joseph Losey as director and Edmond Birnbrier as radio adaptor.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes.

This version dramatizes [[work|work.words.20c08dad2eb905e0|Love at First Flight]]. Charles Spaulding is credited as author, Otis Carney is credited as author, and Edmond Birnbrier adapted it for radio.

grh_37bb2ee60c9f83fa1540.title: Echo of Madness
paragraphs: A frightened woman named Judy arrives at an isolated hotel where the staff and a man named Bruce seem to be conspiring against her, forcing her to remain while recreating disturbing sights, sounds and sensations. The apparent persecution is actually a carefully staged psychiatric treatment. Judy is Bruce's wife, and a train crash at the beginning of their honeymoon caused traumatic amnesia that erased him and the event from her memory. Re-experiencing the champagne, cold room, army blanket and passing train finally breaks through the block, restores her identity and reunites the newlyweds.

grh_372e1816cda90279c198.title: Miss Cinderella
paragraphs: Lucinda Brown escapes an ordinary life by losing herself in the story of Cinderella and its prince searching for the girl who fits a lost slipper. Her own day begins to echo the fairy tale when Joe from McCloskey's shoe store tracks her down through a shoe and arrives just as she reaches the same scene in the book. Lucinda and Joe recognize the comic parallel, and the modern Cinderella story ends with the suggestion that a girl can still find her prince in the most everyday place.

grh_3741d19b0255936c191b.title: The Schumann Story
paragraphs: This musical biography follows composer Robert Schumann and pianist Clara Wieck as their friendship and shared music grow into love. Clara's father, Friedrich Wieck, opposes Robert and refuses permission for the marriage, forcing the couple to seek relief from the courts.
